h1: The 6 Best Murphy Beds for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Home Office Murphy Beds: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Murphy beds and kits for home offices, sorted by size, storage, build effort, finish and desk friendliness.
summary: The Create-A-Bed Queen Deluxe kit is the best Murphy bed for a home office: a vertical queen mechanism with gas piston assist that you build into your own cabinet, so a desk can fit your exact room, for $200 to $500. The AMERLIFE is the best ready-made cabinet with storage, and the budget hardware kit costs $100 to $200.
intro: The surprise in this category is that almost no Murphy bed in a box includes a desk. You get a bed that folds into a cabinet, and the office half is up to you, so the real question is how much of the build you want to take on yourself. A kit gives you freedom and a project. A ready-made cabinet gives you a finished wall and a desk problem.

We went through six Murphy beds and kits, drawing on spec sheets and what owners report about assembly and daily use. We ranked them on build flexibility, storage, size, finish and how well each leaves room for a working desk. Two near-duplicate Hlivelood variants were left out so every pick offers something different, and two of the six are hardware-only kits.

products.name: Create-A-Bed Queen Size Deluxe Murphy Bed Kit, Vertical
products.verdict: Hardware you build into your own cabinet, so the desk can fit your exact room.
products.description:
The Create-A-Bed Deluxe kit is a queen vertical wall bed mechanism with gas piston lift assist. It is sold as hardware only, so you build the cabinet yourself, and a step-by-step installation guide is included. It sells in the $200 to $500 range before lumber. Gas pistons carry most of the bed's weight, so folding it takes one hand and no slamming.

It ranks first because building the cabinet means you can add a deep desk, monitor arms and shelves sized to your room, which no ready-made unit offers. The cost is time and tools. Against the AMERLIFE, it asks more work but returns a fit that a boxed cabinet cannot match.

Buy it if you are comfortable with carpentry and want an office that fits your exact space. The caveats are that you build the cabinet and lumber costs extra. Skip it if you want to open a box and be done.
products.idealFor: DIY builders wanting a custom office.
products.skipIf: You want a ready made cabinet.

products.name: AMERLIFE Queen Murphy Bed with Storage and Charging Station
products.verdict: A finished cabinet bed with side storage and a built in charging station.
products.description:
The AMERLIFE is a queen cabinet Murphy bed with side storage compartments, a built-in charging station and MDF cabinet construction. It has a foldable platform base and sells in the $200 to $500 range. Side compartments hold books, linens or office supplies, so the cabinet doubles as a storage wall around a closed bed.

It ranks second because it needs no cabinet building, which makes it the quickest way to a guest bed in an office. The charging station and side storage are handy, but you will need a separate desk because the cabinet itself does not provide one. Against the kits, it costs about the same as the Create-A-Bed and spares the carpentry.

Choose it if you want built-in storage and a guest bed without a DIY build. The caveat is MDF construction and no desk. Skip it if you want a built-in desk.
products.idealFor: Guest bed with storage, no DIY.
products.skipIf: You want a built in desk.

products.name: Yoobure Queen Murphy Bed with Charging Station, Rattan Frame with Storage Drawers
products.verdict: A rattan front cabinet that still looks like furniture when the bed is up.
products.description:
The Yoobure is a queen cabinet bed with a rattan front, a charging station, storage drawers and a foldable platform base. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. A rattan front reads as decor, not hardware, so the room still looks like an office or living space when the bed is stowed.

It ranks third because it matches the AMERLIFE on function while leaning on style. The rattan front looks more like furniture than a bed cabinet, which helps in a shared living space or studio. Against the AMERLIFE, it swaps open compartments for pull-out drawers.

Choose it for a studio or living room where the office is part of a room that guests also see. The caveat is that style comes before function, and there is no desk. Skip it if you want a built-in desk.
products.skipIf: You want a built in desk.

products.name: Queen Size Murphy Bed Hardware Kit, Vertical Wall Bed Frame with Gas Pistons
products.verdict: A cheaper DIY kit with three build guides and gas pistons.
products.description:
This kit is a queen vertical wall bed mechanism with gas pistons, three step-by-step build guides and North American manufacturing. It is hardware only and sells in the $100 to $200 range. Three build guides help a first-time builder choose a cabinet layout, which lowers the risk of a half-finished project.

It ranks fourth because it offers the same DIY flexibility as the Create-A-Bed at a lower price, but with less information on the lift hardware. The multiple build guides help beginners. Against the ready-made cabinets, you save on the mechanism and pay in time and lumber.

Choose it if you want to build a custom desk and bed combo and want to save on the mechanism. The caveat is that cabinet cost is extra. Skip it if you do not own basic tools.
products.skipIf: You do not own basic tools.

products.name: Hlivelood Queen Size Murphy Bed with 2 LED Lights, Gas Struts, Rustic White
products.verdict: A queen cabinet bed with two built in LED lights.
products.description:
The Hlivelood queen bed has two built-in LED lights, gas strut fold assist, a rustic white cabinet finish and needs no box spring. It sells at $500+. Lights built into the cabinet replace a separate lamp, which frees desk or shelf space in a small office.

It ranks fifth because the lights are the main extra and it sits in the top price bracket, higher than the ready-made options above. White reflects light into a small room. Against the AMERLIFE, it adds lighting and gas struts but no storage or charging.

Buy it if you want lighting in the cabinet itself and have the budget. The caveat is the price and the missing desk. Skip it if you are on a budget.

products.name: LIVAUVEAD Twin Size Murphy Bed with Charging Station and Drawer, White
products.verdict: A twin size cabinet bed for rooms where width is the limit.
products.description:
The LIVAUVEAD is a twin cabinet Murphy bed with a built-in charging station, a single storage drawer, a white finish and a foldable platform base. It sells in the $200 to $500 range. A twin takes the least floor width of the group, which leaves a wall segment free for a desk.

It ranks last because a twin bed is too small for many guests, though it needs the narrowest wall. The drawer and charging port add some convenience. Against the AMERLIFE, it has less storage but a footprint that works in a tight room.

Choose it for a small, single-occupant home office where room width is the tightest constraint. The caveat is a bed too small for couples. Skip it if you host couples.

whatMatters.detail: Very few Murphy beds include a desk, so the question is whether the bed lets you add one. Hardware kits let you build a desk into the cabinet, while ready-made units need a separate desk placed nearby. Read the listing for the word desk and decide if you can live without one.

A kit gives you only the lift mechanism and you build the cabinet. A ready-made cabinet arrives with panels and hardware to assemble. Kits cost less for the hardware but more in time, and require tools. The Create-A-Bed and budget kit are hardware only, while the AMERLIFE, Yoobure and Hlivelood ship as cabinets.

Twin saves floor width, while queen fits couples but takes a wider wall. Measure the wall and the floor depth when open. Compare the listing's dimensions with your room, and remember that the open bed claims space that a desk chair also needs. Allow clearance on both sides for a person to get in.

Gas pistons or struts carry most of the bed's weight so you can fold it with one hand. Weak mechanisms feel heavy or slam down. Look for gas piston or gas strut in the title, as on the Create-A-Bed and Hlivelood. A dependable lift makes daily use painless, and a weak one turns folding the bed into a chore you start to avoid.

MDF and particleboard are common in ready-made cabinets, while a DIY build can use solid wood. Material affects weight, sturdiness and look. Check the listing for the cabinet material, and note that the AMERLIFE is MDF while kits leave the choice to you. Solid lumber adds weight, which gas pistons must balance.

faq.q: Do Murphy beds include a desk?
faq.a: Almost none do. Kits let you build one into the cabinet, and ready-made units like the AMERLIFE or Yoobure need a separate desk. Plan one on an adjacent wall, out of the bed's swing arc.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Ignoring ceiling and floor clearance. Measure the open bed's depth and the wall width before you order, and leave room for a desk chair. A bed that opens into your desk is a daily frustration, so mark its footprint with tape on the floor.

faq.q: Is a DIY kit worth it over a ready made bed?
faq.a: If you want a built-in desk and own tools, yes. If you want speed, the cabinet is easier. The Create-A-Bed gives the most freedom, but it costs weekends and lumber. Budget realistic time and add the cost of the cabinet materials.
Ready-made cabinets need several hours and often two people. Kits need cabinet carpentry and wall anchoring. Ask a friend to help lift panels, and plan a full weekend for a first build.

faq.q: Does the bed need to be anchored?
faq.a: Wall bed mechanisms should be secured to studs following the maker's guide, especially for kits like the Create-A-Bed. Never rely on drywall alone, because a falling bed frame is a serious injury risk. Use the hardware in the kit.
Yes, in most cases. Check the listing for mattress size and thickness limits, since a mattress that is too thick will not fold into the cabinet. A firmer, thinner mattress also makes folding easier.

finalTake: Buy the Create-A-Bed kit if you are comfortable with carpentry and want a custom desk beside or under the bed. Take the AMERLIFE for a finished cabinet with storage and the Yoobure when looks matter. The budget hardware kit saves on the mechanism, and the Hlivelood adds built-in lights. The LIVAUVEAD twin suits narrow rooms. Plan the desk before you pick a bed.
